nodes.description: Owner address of the contract; set to msg.sender in the Owned constructor and guarded by onlyOwner.
Pending new owner set by transferOwnership and consumed/cleared by acceptOwnership.
ERC20 token symbol, initialized to 1TOKEN in the constructor.
ERC20 token name, initialized to 1 Token in the constructor.
Token decimals, fixed at 18 in the constructor.
Total token supply set to 1000000000000000000 (1 token with 18 decimals) and returned by totalSupply().
Mapping of address to token balance; written by transfer/transferFrom and read by balanceOf/totalSupply.
Nested mapping owner=>spender=>amount used for ERC20 allowances.
Pure helper adding two uints and requiring the result is not smaller than the input (overflow guard).
Pure helper subtracting b from a and requiring b <= a (underflow guard).
Pure helper multiplying two uints with a division-based overflow guard.
Pure helper dividing a by b after requiring b > 0.
Owned constructor that assigns msg.sender as the initial owner.
onlyOwner function storing _newOwner as the pending owner.
Function that requires msg.sender == newOwner, emits OwnershipTransferred, moves ownership and clears newOwner.
Token constructor setting symbol, name, decimals, _totalSupply and pre-funding the deployer address, emitting Transfer.
Constant function returning _totalSupply - balances[address(0)].
Constant function returning balances[tokenOwner].
ERC20 transfer: debits msg.sender and credits to using SafeMath and emits Transfer.
ERC20 approve: writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] = tokens and emits Approval.
ERC20 transferFrom: debits from balance and allowance of msg.sender, credits to, using SafeMath.
Constant function returning allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
Sets allowance then makes an external callback to spender.receiveApproval(msg.sender, tokens, this, data).
Payable fallback function that immediately reverts, rejecting plain Ether transfers.
onlyOwner function that calls transfer(owner, tokens) on an arbitrary token contract address.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership, balance keys, allowance keys and callback arguments.
External call to an attacker-supplied spender contract via receiveApproval, executed inside approveAndCall with attacker-controlled data.
External call to an arbitrary token contract (ERC20Interface.transfer) inside transferAnyERC20Token.
Unsigned addition a + b performed before the overflow require, relying on the SafeMath guard.
Unsigned subtraction a - b performed after the underflow require in safeSub.
Unsigned multiplication a * b performed before the division-based overflow check.
Unsigned division a / b guarded by require(b > 0).
Recipient address parameter of transfer.
Amount parameter of transfer, used in the sender/recipient balance arithmetic.
Spender address parameter of approve, used as the second key of the allowed mapping.
Approved amount parameter of approve.
Source address parameter of transferFrom whose balance and allowance are debited.
Destination address parameter of transferFrom.
Amount parameter of transferFrom used in balance and allowance arithmetic.
Spender/target contract parameter of approveAndCall that is also the external call target.
Approved amount parameter of approveAndCall forwarded to the external callback.
Arbitrary calldata parameter forwarded verbatim to the external receiveApproval call.
Arbitrary token contract address parameter used as the external call target.
Amount parameter of transferAnyERC20Token sent to owner from the target token contract.
Address parameter stored into the newOwner state variable.
Local return variable holding the sum computed in safeAdd.

edges.reason: Owned constructor reads msg.sender to establish the initial owner.
msg.sender is assigned directly to the owner state variable.
Constructor writes owner state variable from msg.sender.
onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender with owner before setting newOwner.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner to transfer ownership.
transfer uses msg.sender as the balance key that is debited.
approve stores the allowance under allowed[msg.sender][spender].
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender whose allowance is debited.
approveAndCall forwards msg.sender into an external contract call.
msg.sender is passed as the first argument of the external receiveApproval callback.
OneToken constructor assigns the fixed initial value of _totalSupply.
OneToken constructor credits the full supply to the fixed deployer address in balances.
totalSupply returns _totalSupply.
totalSupply subtracts balances[address(0)] from _totalSupply.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping for tokenOwner.
transfer debits sender and credits recipient in the balances mapping through SafeMath routines.
transfer calls safeSub to decrement the sender balance.
transfer calls safeAdd to increment the recipient balance.
approve writes the requested amount into the allowed mapping.
transferFrom debits the from balance and credits the to balance.
transferFrom decrements the caller allowance in the allowed mapping.
transferFrom calls safeSub for balance and allowance decrements.
transferFrom calls safeAdd for the recipient credit.
allowance returns allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call.
approveAndCall invokes receiveApproval on the caller-supplied spender contract after updating state.
transferAnyERC20Token invokes transfer on an arbitrary token contract supplied by the owner.
transferAnyERC20Token sends the pulled tokens to the owner address.
onlyOwner restricts transferAnyERC20Token to the address stored from msg.sender.
transferOwnership stores the supplied address into newOwner.
acceptOwnership reads newOwner for the caller check and later clears it to address(0).
acceptOwnership commits ownership by writing newOwner into owner.
safeAdd performs the raw unsigned addition a + b that is only guarded afterwards.
safeSub performs the raw unsigned subtraction a - b after the underflow require.
safeMul performs the raw unsigned multiplication a * b before the overflow check.
safeDiv performs the unsigned division a / b guarded by require(b > 0).
Recipient parameter to is credited in the balances mapping by transfer.
Amount parameter tokens is subtracted from the sender and added to the recipient.
tokens flows into the safeSub call that debits the sender balance.
tokens flows into the safeAdd call that credits the recipient balance.
spender parameter is used as the second key of allowed[msg.sender][spender].
tokens parameter is stored verbatim as the approved amount.
from parameter keys the balances mapping entry that is debited.
to parameter keys the balances mapping entry that is credited.
tokens parameter is the amount removed from balance and allowance in transferFrom.
spender parameter is both the allowance key and the external call target.
tokens parameter becomes the allowance and is forwarded to the callback.
data parameter is attacker-controlled calldata passed straight through approveAndCall.
Arbitrary data is supplied to the external receiveApproval call.
spender parameter determines which external contract receives the callback.
tokenAddress parameter selects the ERC20 contract whose transfer is invoked.
tokens parameter is the amount requested from the external token contract.
tokenAddress parameter is used as the target of the external ERC20 transfer call.
_newOwner parameter is written into the newOwner state variable.
Local c stores the computed sum and is returned by safeAdd.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter only exists as the recipient key for the balance credit inside transfer; it has no independent role and can be folded into the function node.
The parameter is consumed only by the SafeMath debit/credit operations of transfer and is merged into that function node.
The parameter is used only as a key when writing the allowed mapping inside approve.
The parameter is written directly to the allowance mapping inside approve and carries no separate semantics.
The parameter only selects the balances mapping entry debited by transferFrom.
The parameter only selects the balances mapping entry credited by transferFrom.
The parameter is used exclusively in the SafeMath balance and allowance updates of transferFrom.
The parameter is the target of the external callback and therefore belongs with the unsafe external call node rather than a stand-alone parameter.
The parameter becomes the allowance and is forwarded to the callback, so it is absorbed by the enclosing function.
The parameter is arbitrary calldata passed verbatim to the external callback, so it is merged into the unsafe external call node.
The parameter is the call target of the external ERC20 transfer and is merged into that unsafe operation.
The parameter is only the amount forwarded to the external transfer inside the function.
The parameter is stored directly into newOwner and has no independent dataflow role.
The local variable only holds the return value of the addition, which is fully described by the safeAdd function node.
